2027-05-23.title: First Sunday after Pentecost
readings: The manna ceases; they eat the produce of the land
Filled with the spirit of the Lord
Plans for your welfare, a future with hope
The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily
2027-05-23.alt: Season of Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was Vocation Day.
2027-05-23.verse: By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
theo: The season of Pentecost is the season of the Church's life in the Spirit. If Pentecost was the planting, these Sundays are about the fruit. St Paul names it: “the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control… If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.”

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells the parable of the sower. Seed falls on the path, on rock, among thorns and on good soil. “As for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.” The Spirit sows; we must become good soil: attentive, deep, free from the thorns of worry and riches.

In the Gospel the crowds follow Jesus after the multiplication of loaves, looking for more bread. He tells them: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.” When they ask what work God wants, he answers: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.” “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” Israel's manna stopped when they reached the promised land; the true Bread will never fail.

Jeremiah gives a word of hope to people in exile: “I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope… When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart.” God has a plan, a vocation, for each of us; the Spirit leads us to discover it.
conn: Joshua 5:12: the manna ceased when Israel ate the produce of the land; Jesus is the true bread from heaven (John 6:32–33).
Exodus 12: God's people go out from slavery; the Spirit leads us from the slavery of the flesh to freedom (Galatians 5:16–18).
Acts 17:11: they examined the Scriptures daily; the good soil is a heart that studies the Word.
Micah 3:8: the prophet filled with the spirit of the Lord to speak truth.
altar: “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” In the Holy Qurbono we receive the bread that endures for eternal life, and the Spirit makes us bear fruit.
outline: Point 1 · The fruit of the Spirit
Love, joy, peace… a portrait of Christ in us.
The sower: hearing, holding fast, patient endurance.
Work for the food of eternal life.
Vocation Day: God's plan for each life.
“If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.”
live: Pick one fruit of the Spirit (patience, kindness…) to practise deliberately this week.
Like the Bereans, read a short passage of Scripture each day.
Pray for young people discerning priesthood, religious life or marriage.
fathers: Be good soil: do not let the Word fall on the path of a careless heart, on the rock of a hard heart, or among the thorns of worldly cares (Sermon 73).
The fruit of the Spirit is not something we produce alone; the Spirit works in us, but we must cooperate, as soil receives rain and bears grain (Commentary on Galatians 5).
magis: The fruits of the Spirit are perfections that the Holy Spirit forms in us as the first fruits of eternal glory.
Meditation on the Word; the parable of the sower.
Vocations to marriage and the ordained ministry at the service of communion.
saints: 26 May: St Philip Neri. Weekdays of the season of Pentecost.
2027-05-23.prayer: Holy Spirit, sower of the Word, make our hearts good soil. Bear in us the fruit of love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control; feed us with the bread from heaven, and show each of us the plan you have for our lives. Amen.

quick: After Pentecost: the Spirit bears fruit in us.
Be good soil: hear the Word, hold it fast, bear fruit with patience.
Work for the bread that endures: believe in the One God has sent.
2027-05-23.action: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and practise it deliberately this week.
2027-05-23.question: What kind of soil is my heart for God's Word?
2027-05-23.special: First Sunday after Pentecost. (In 2025–26 also Vocation Day; check the collection.)
illus: Kerala farmers know that seed sown on laterite rock dries up, while the same seed in the paddy field brings a harvest. The difference is the soil, not the seed. The Spirit sows the same Word in all of us.

family.explain: The Holy Spirit helps good things grow in us, like fruit on a tree: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
family.intention: We pray that the fruit of the Spirit may grow in our family.
family.ask: Ask: “Which fruit of the Spirit will each of us practise this week?”

kidsaint: A Syro-Malabar sister from Thrissur who visited poor families, cared for the sick and the dying, and founded the Congregation of the Holy Family. The fruit of the Spirit was seen in her kindness. Lesson: let your kindness show God's love.
term: The season after Pentecost when the Church, filled with the Spirit, grows and bears fruit. In the Syro-Malankara year it leads into the season of the Transfiguration.
termMore: The Friday after Pentecost, when the lectionary reads the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk” (Acts 3:6).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we celebrated Pentecost, the coming of the Holy Spirit. Today we ask: what difference does the Spirit make? St Paul answers: the Spirit bears fruit. “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.” Read that list slowly; it is a portrait of Jesus, and of what he wants to grow in us.

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells of a sower. Some seed falls on the path, some on rock, some among thorns, and some on good soil. The seed is the same; the soil makes the difference. The good soil is “an honest and good heart” that hears the Word, holds it fast and bears fruit with patience. The Spirit keeps sowing; are we good soil?

In John's Gospel the crowds look for Jesus because he gave them bread. He tells them: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.” And he says: “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” That bread is given to us at this altar.

Today is also a day to pray for vocations. Jeremiah says: “I know the plans I have for you, plans for your welfare, to give you a future with hope.” God has a plan for every young person here: priesthood, religious life, marriage, a mission. Let us ask the Spirit to show it, and let us choose this week one fruit of the Spirit to practise. Amen.
kids: Children, when a tree is healthy, it gives fruit. When the Holy Spirit lives in us, we give fruit too: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness!
Jesus told a story about a farmer sowing seed. The seed that fell on good soil grew a big harvest. Our hearts should be good soil for God's Word.
Which fruit will you grow this week? Kindness? Patience? Let's say: “Holy Spirit, help me grow good fruit!”

intro: Theme: “The Spirit bears fruit in good soil.”
After Pentecost the Church asks what difference the Spirit makes. The answer is fruit: a heart that receives the Word, a life that shows love and joy, and a people fed by the bread that endures.

sub: The seed is the word of God; the soil is the human heart.
Good soil hears the word, holds it fast and bears fruit with patience.
Jeremiah: those who seek God with all their heart will find him.
q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart.
But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again each evening this week and keep one word in your heart.

sub: Micah was filled with the spirit of the Lord to speak truth with courage.
St Paul names the fruit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.
q: But as for me, I am filled with power, with the spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and practise it deliberately each day this week.

points.h: Bread that endures and a plan for each life
sub: Jesus urges us to work for the food that endures for eternal life.
God has plans for our welfare, a future with hope: every life has a vocation.
The Spirit leads young people to discover their call: priesthood, religious life, marriage.
q: For surely I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you.
points.apply: Pray for vocations, and encourage a young person to listen to God's call.

concl: The Spirit sows, nourishes and makes us fruitful.
Let us be good soil, bear his fruit, and feed on the bread that endures.
2027-05-23.resolve: Each night this week, examine: which fruit of the Spirit did I show today?
